title: Generative deep learning discovers the RIPK1 inhibitor RI-962 with an unreported scaffold
summary: A target-conditioned generative deep-learning model based on a distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network generated a tailored compound library that was screened for RIPK1 inhibition. The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
ai_technology: Generative deep-learning distribution-learning conditional recurrent neural network (GDL cRNN)
organization: State Key Laboratory of Biotherapy and Cancer Center, West China Hospital, Sichuan University; West China School of Pharmacy, Sichuan University

evidence.tested: The study reports RI-962 as a potent inhibitor with a previously unreported scaffold, validated in vitro for protection from necroptosis and in vivo in two inflammatory models.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is preclinical: cellular necroptosis assays and two inflammatory mouse models do not establish human efficacy or safety. The paper identifies one leading molecule from a generated library; it does not validate generative-model performance across targets generally.
evidence.ai_role: The GDL cRNN generated a target-tailored virtual compound library; virtual screening and subsequent chemical synthesis and bioactivity assays selected RI-962. This provides direct experimental testing of a model-generated molecule rather than a prediction-only hit.
